slides.title: Price went up?|Why hotel rates move
slides.body: Same room, different price. Here's why.

slides.title: Demand.
slides.body: When many people search the same dates, rates rise. Quiet dates, lower rates.

slides.title: The day of the week.
slides.body: Business hotels are often busier Monday to Thursday, leisure spots at the weekend.

slides.title: Local events.
slides.body: A trade fair, a concert or a big match can fill a city's hotels fast.

slides.title: The season.
slides.body: Summer on the coast, ski weeks in the mountains. High season costs more.

slides.title: Length of stay.
slides.body: Some hotels set minimum stays or different rates for longer bookings.

slides.title: Who sells the room.
slides.body: The same room is sold by many suppliers at different rates. We compare 280+ of them.

slides.title: Found your dates?
slides.body: Compare the rates on Resapass. Link in bio.

slides.title: Checkout day|6 things to do first
slides.body: Leave the hotel with everything you came with.

slides.title: Ask for late checkout the day before.
slides.body: It's easier for the hotel to say yes when it can plan for it.

slides.title: Open the safe.
slides.body: Passports and jewellery are the classic things left behind.

slides.title: Check the plugs.
slides.body: Chargers and adapters love to stay in the wall.

slides.title: Read the bill before you pay.
slides.body: Minibar, breakfast, city tax. Ask if a line doesn't look right.

slides.title: Ask for an invoice.
slides.body: Travelling for work? Get it at the desk, it's harder to get later.

slides.title: Leave your bags at reception.
slides.body: Late flight? Many hotels keep luggage for a few hours after checkout.

slides.title: Next trip planned?
slides.body: Find your next hotel on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
The last morning goes fast. Here's what to do before you hand back the key.

Ask for late checkout the day before, open the safe, check the plugs for chargers, read the bill, ask for an invoice if you travel for work and leave your bags at reception if your flight is late.

slides.title: Florence|where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 neighbourhoods, 5 different trips.

slides.title: Duomo & centre
slides.body: The cathedral, the Uffizi and Ponte Vecchio, all within a short walk.

slides.title: Oltrarno
slides.body: Across the river: workshops, the Pitti Palace and lively Piazza Santo Spirito.

slides.title: Santa Croce
slides.body: Around the basilica, near Sant'Ambrogio market, with plenty of bars.

slides.title: San Niccolò
slides.body: Small streets below Piazzale Michelangelo and its view over the city.

slides.title: Santa Maria Novella
slides.body: Next to the main station, handy for Pisa, Bologna and Rome.

slides.title: Which one is yours?
slides.body: Compare Florence hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Florence is small, but each side of the river feels different.

First visit? The centre around the Duomo. Workshops and a local piazza? Oltrarno. Food and evenings out? Santa Croce. Quiet streets and views? San Niccolò. Day trips by train? Santa Maria Novella.

slides.title: Pack lighter|the hotel often has these
slides.body: Leave them out of the suitcase.

slides.title: A hairdryer.
slides.body: Most hotel rooms have one. Check the room details to be sure.

slides.title: Towels.
slides.body: Bath towels are standard. Some hotels also lend pool or beach towels.

slides.title: Shampoo and shower gel.
slides.body: Usually in the bathroom. Bring your own only if you're picky.

slides.title: An iron.
slides.body: Often available on request from reception, if not already in the room.

slides.title: A toothbrush or razor.
slides.body: Forgot one? Many receptions keep spare kits.

slides.title: An umbrella.
slides.body: Some hotels lend them at the door on rainy days. Just ask.

slides.title: Lighter bag, same trip.

caption:
Your suitcase is heavier than it needs to be.
